title: What is Conversion Rate? Formula, Benchmarks & Denominators
meta_description: Conversion rate is completions divided by a denominator you choose. The formula, the medians that matter, and why the denominator decides the answer.

visuals.alt: Six conversion reference points: median free-to-paid across products, median day-one return rate, hard paywall against freemium download-to-paid, average freemium-to-paid across 80-plus products, the win rate of price localisation experiments and India's cost-per-install ratio, each row carrying its source and verification date
visuals.caption: Conversion reference points, each row sourced. Verified 30 September 2026.

faq.q: What is a good conversion rate?
faq.a: The question has no answer without a denominator. Median free-to-paid across products is 8%. Download-to-paid within 35 days is 2.1% for freemium apps and 10.7% for hard paywalls. Those are all conversion rates and none is comparable to another.

faq.q: Why did my conversion rate improve without any change?
faq.a: Usually the denominator moved. Cutting low-intent traffic raises conversion while lowering total conversions. Both effects are real, and only one of them is good news.

faq.q: What is the highest-yield conversion experiment?
faq.a: Price localisation wins 62.3% of experiments, the highest win rate of any test type. For a product selling across markets it beats most copy and layout work.

unique_value_statement: Treats the denominator as the definition rather than a footnote, lining up four published conversion medians that are routinely compared and are not comparable, and carries a worked case where one funnel had seven separate multiplicative leaks.
